taste.name: Absorb, Don't Compete — the Gray Canvas
taste.trigger: Laying out a grid where nearly every cell is a different, uncontrolled film still with clashing color and tone
taste.decision: Chose a flat warm mid-gray page background (#EAEAEA) over pure white or pure black
taste.reason: White would wash out stills and amplify contrast clashes between neighbors; black would tip the page into cinema-viewer mode instead of a browsing surface. Mid-gray stays neutral enough that no single still can dominate it
evidence: not present in top text or accent color lists

taste.name: No Elevation, By Design
taste.trigger: Building a repeating grid-cell component that renders thousands of times across a 417-page catalog
taste.decision: Chose zero border-radius, zero border, and no perceivable shadow over any card elevation treatment
taste.reason: Elevation is a cost paid once by the designer but re-rendered and re-perceived thousands of times by the user; flatness lets the grid recede so the artwork carries the page rather than a UI chrome effect competing with it at scale
evidence: no bordered card shape detected by the extractor at all

taste.name: Metadata as Skin, Not Furniture
taste.trigger: Needing to show title, director, and country/year on a cell fully occupied by a 16:9 image with no reserved caption space
taste.decision: Chose a bottom-left text overlay on a dark scrim directly over the image, over a separate caption bar below the image
taste.reason: A caption bar under every cell would shrink the actual artwork by roughly a fifth to make room for three lines of small text, repeated across hundreds of pages; overlaying keeps full image size and treats the text like credits printed on a lobby card
evidence: white text (#FFFFFF, count 102) dominates the text-color sample
12px/14px/700-weight metadata block sits inside the image bounds, not below it

taste.name: One Blue, Never Spent on the Content Itself
taste.trigger: Having a single brand accent color while the grid already supplies its own color signal from hundreds of unrelated film stills
taste.decision: Chose to spend #001489 exclusively on UI state — active tab, links, CTA — over using it to color-code genres, badges, or tags on the grid itself
taste.reason: If the accent bled into content (colored genre badges on every still), it would compete with the artwork and dilute its own meaning; kept scarce, the one time it shows up mid-hover it reads unambiguously as 'this is an action,' not decoration
evidence: #001489 occupies ~0.6% of visible area despite 38 occurrences
